Thailand Fund Efficient Frontier

Efficient frontier of your fund universe

X = annualised StdDev (%) · Y = annualised mean return (%) · long-only, fully invested · computed live from the filters below

How to use

  • Build the universe with the filters (Main / Shelf / AMC / Risk; combined with AND). Sub-category and Risk are tick lists: unticked items are left out (money market and short-term bond start unticked), or list funds in Input. Once Input has funds, the frontier uses only those funds and the filters pause until you clear Input. With every filter on All and Input empty, the universe is all funds.
  • Input takes one fund at a time from the suggestion list, or a pasted list of fund codes separated by commas or new lines.
  • Pick the data window — 1Y, 3Y or 5Y of weekly returns. Funds without that much history drop out (listed in the Universe table).
  • Hover any point on the purple frontier line to see its fund weights. Click to lock it into the Selected portfolio table.
  • Max weight / fund: type a % (e.g. 25) to cap any single fund; leave it empty for no cap. Untick a fund in the Universe table to exclude it.
  • Return model: Historical uses past average returns; Black-Litterman starts from market-implied returns and lets you add views (e.g. “Global Equity = 8%” or “US Equity beats Japan Equity by 2%”) with a confidence level.
  • Max funds: type a number (e.g. 5) so every portfolio on the line holds at most that many funds; the dashed line shows the frontier with no limit.
Methodology & data
Inputs: weekly total-return series for 2,855 share classes (dividend classes use the sister Acc class, or reinvested SEC dividend history — same treatment as the Risk-Return dashboard), sampled every 7 days back from the latest NAV date. Weekly rather than daily because Thai feeder funds price a day behind their master fund, which distorts daily correlations.
Expected return = mean weekly return × 52 (arithmetic, annualised). Risk = weekly StdDev × √52. Covariance = sample covariance with correlations shrunk toward zero (Schäfer–Strimmer intensity, shown in the status line) so the result stays stable when the universe is large relative to the number of weeks.
Optimisation: for each point, minimise portfolio variance for its level of expected return, subject to weights ≥ 0, sum = 100%, and the max-weight cap. Solved in your browser each time the universe changes; usually 80 funds are optimised at once (more, up to 120, when a low max weight needs them, when Input / ticked funds exceed 80, or when the screening runs out of room). The working set retains the highest-return funds needed for the max-weight cap, then your Input / ticked funds and the best Sharpe ratios. All eligible funds share one covariance estimate. Other funds are screened for feasible weight transfers that improve sampled frontier points. This is an approximation: small improvements or improvements between sampled points may remain; the status reports unresolved screening candidates.
Black-Litterman (Return model switch): expected returns start from what the market implies — the funds' AUM weights are treated as the market portfolio, and returns are backed out so that portfolio has the Market Sharpe you set (default 0.4): Π = δ·Σ·w, δ = Sharpe ÷ market SD. Your views (a group's return, or one group beating another, each group AUM-weighted) shift those returns by an amount that depends on your confidence (τ = 0.05; view uncertainty 4× / 1× / ¼× of the prior's for Low / Medium / High). The frontier is then built from these returns with the same covariance; the grey dashed line shows the same funds with historical returns.
Max funds (optional) limits how many funds each frontier portfolio may hold. Exact solutions are combinatorial, so each point keeps its largest holdings, re-optimises their weights and tries one-for-one swaps with the most promising other funds; the dashed line is the frontier without the limit, so the gap shows what the limit costs.
Max Sharpe uses the risk-free rate you enter. One class per fund uses only the largest share class of each fund by default, because sibling classes have near-identical returns; the other classes stay in the Universe table unticked, and ticking one adds it.
Caveat: the frontier is built from historical returns, so it favours whatever performed best in the chosen window. Use it to understand diversification trade-offs, not as a forecast or a recommendation.
Source: Thailand SEC Open Data API (api.sec.or.th). NAV data as of 19 Oct 2026.
